- When sentiment is positive (≥0.4) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >72.5), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +2–3% above peak or use 3-day moving average to dampen momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to account for lagged support.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or weak; apply 0.8–1.2% upward bias for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment spikes to 1.0 (strong bullish), model often overreacts; apply 10–15% downward correction to prevent overbought overcorrection.
- Forecast mean reversion is stronger in 10–15 day horizon; if model is above 72.5 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce by 1–2% per day until price stabilizes.
